info.title: Shuttle daemon API, stable tier
info.description: The routes a UI other than the board can build on. `info.version` is the API level, the integer `GET /api/v1/version` reports as `api_level`: adding a route or an optional field leaves it alone, removing or renaming anything described here raises it by one. Response objects may carry fields this document does not name; a client ignores them. Everything under /api/v1 that is absent from this document is internal and moves with the board.

get.summary: This document, as served by the daemon answering.
get.description: Read the stable operations and shapes supported by this daemon. The document version is the API level reported by /version.
Reports the build, host, terminal backend, API level and independent CLI contract level, even during boot. With origin, reads that host instead; readiness does not imply fresh launches are released.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

200.description: This daemon's identity, build and readiness, or the named host's when origin is given (relayed with its own status).

502.description: The named host did not answer; detail says why.

get.summary: Read a host’s configured and discovered remotes.
get.description: Joins normalized remote configuration to cached reachability and remote build stamps, without probing hosts on demand. A configuration read failure is still 200 with error set and an empty remotes list.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

200.description: The host's remotes. When the fleet file cannot be read, error says why and remotes is empty.

400.description: origin names no known host; the body carries ok false.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the named host.

503.description: Boot is incomplete or held; no action is attempted.

get.description: Returns exact shuttle://HOST/HARNESS/NATIVE_ID addresses across the fleet, or only this host when local=true. Discovery failures become gaps in a 200 response rather than discarding successful sessions.

parameters.name: local
parameters.description: "true" lists only this daemon's sessions; "false" or absent lists every reachable host's.

200.description: Sessions found, plus a gap for each host or harness that could not be listed.

get.description: Combines owner-published rows and per-origin freshness; unreachable owners retain stale cached rows. Carry a row’s origin into subsequent owner-routed requests; column and turn are present for Shuttle constitutions, not necessarily ordinary dated notes.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Send the ETag from a prior response. A match returns 304 with no body.

200.description: Every host's rows, each stamped with its origin, and the freshness of each origin. Carries an ETag.

ETag.description: Weak validator over the visible feed.

503.description: Boot is incomplete or held; no action is attempted.

get.summary: Read one fiber from its owner.
get.description: Reads by UID or slash-separated namespace path; encode each path segment separately. body=true includes Markdown in fiber.body; omitted origin can infer a configured owner from shuttle.host, but local reads use felt’s convenient lookup, so a missing namespace path can resolve by its leaf name instead of returning 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Fiber UID or namespace path, including nested segments.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: "true" or "1" includes the Markdown body in fiber.body; any other value or absence omits it.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

parameters.name: routed
parameters.description: Set by a daemon forwarding the read: "1" or "true" answers from this host even when the fiber's shuttle.host names another. Clients omit it.

200.description: The fiber in a one-row envelope; fibers[0].fiber holds its frontmatter.

404.description: The host has no fiber with that identifier; error names the host.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the owning host.

503.description: felt could not read the stores (error felt_show_failed, with per-store errors in stores), or boot is incomplete.

post.summary: Launch an agent from a prompt.
post.description: Starts a terminal worker in project_dir on the selected host; the agent files and claims its constitution. The directory must exist on that host; agent and effort are registry selections and chrome requests the browser-enabled axis.

prompt.description: The task for the new agent; must contain non-whitespace text. The agent files and claims its own constitution from it.

project_dir.description: Absolute directory on the selected host where the worker starts; it must already exist there.

agent.description: Agent registry id; null or absent uses the registry default.

effort.description: Effort level, a harness-native token such as low, medium or high; null or absent uses the agent's default.

chrome.description: true launches the agent with the browser (chrome) axis enabled; any other value leaves it off.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

example.prompt: Read the README, list the open TODOs and file a plan for the first one.

200.description: The worker launched; tmux_session names its terminal session. No fiber exists yet: the agent creates it.

400.description: prompt or project_dir is missing or blank, or origin names no known host.

422.description: project_dir does not exist on the host (reason project_dir_missing), the agent, effort and chrome combination is invalid (reason is the validation message), or a launch preflight refused (reason is the refusal tag, message says what to fix).

500.description: The launch failed; reason describes the error.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the owning host; reason is forward_failed and error the cause.

503.description: The terminal backend is not ready (reason backend_not_ready, waiting and retryable true), or boot is incomplete.

post.summary: Create a fiber on its owning host.
post.description: id is a namespace path, not a UID; uid optionally preserves a transferred intrinsic identity. frontmatter defaults to active status, and a Shuttle block is stamped with this host; an active block requires an existing project_dir, and duplicate identities or destinations are refused.

id.description: Namespace path of the new fiber, relative and slash-separated (for example work/new-idea); not a UID. It is placed under its nearest existing ancestor; a new top-level fiber goes to the store holding shuttle.project_dir when that store is polled, else the primary store.

uid.description: A canonical ULID to keep, for a fiber transferred from elsewhere; absent mints a new one. Refused if the owner already has it.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

status.description: open (a draft), active or closed; defaults to active, which arms a shuttle block.

project_dir.description: Worker directory on the owning host; required, and must exist, when status is active.

host.description: Owning host id; absent is stamped with this daemon's id, any other host is refused.

shuttle.description: A Shuttle block. Its host is stamped with this daemon's id when absent and refused when it names another host; a role inside it moves to the top-level role.

tags.description: Free-form tags; non-string items are dropped.

frontmatter.description: Frontmatter for the new fiber. Unlisted keys are written verbatim. status defaults to active.

example.name: Try the new parser
example.body: Swap the parser and compare timings.

200.description: The fiber was written and read back; path is its file on the owner and uid its identity.

400.description: Invalid id, name, uid, status or shuttle block; a duplicate uid or destination; no polled store; a felt write failure; or origin names no known host.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded; error is forward_failed, with origin and detail.

503.description: Boot is incomplete or held; no action is attempted.

post.summary: Launch or resume a fiber’s worker.
post.description: Requests a launch of the constitution's worker now, on its owning host. The fiber is named by fiber_id (not fiber as on /lifecycle). Without force or ad_hoc the fiber must be eligible as for an autonomous dispatch; with either, only host ownership is checked. No flag supplies a missing project directory: a forced start of a block without one answers 422 arm_refused with needs project_dir, and is retried with project_dir. resume_mode chooses previous or fresh context; user_message and images ride the launch. Every response is a JSON object whose dispatched field says whether a worker launched or took the message.

fiber_id.description: The constitution to launch: its UID or namespace path. /dispatch, /deliver and /kill call this field fiber_id; /lifecycle calls it fiber.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

force.description: Bypasses eligibility except host ownership: a closed, draft or not-yet-due constitution launches, and its cooldowns are ignored. Also accepts the strings "true" and "1".

ad_hoc.description: Implies force. A standing constitution's run is recorded as an ad hoc run outside its schedule.

existing_only.description: Never launches. With resume_mode previous and a user_message, types the message into the live worker's terminal; otherwise answers 422 no_live_worker.

release_launch_reservation.description: Before launching, releases the reservation an earlier unresolved launch attempt left (the 409 launch_reserved refusal), if the fiber is eligible.

user_message.description: Text the worker receives as the human's message: in its launch prompt, or typed into the live terminal when resume_mode is previous and a worker is live. Blank counts as absent.

resume_mode.description: previous resumes the prior conversation, or types user_message into a live one; fresh starts a new conversation, stopping a live worker first. Absent or any other value lets the owner decide from how the last run ended.

project_dir.description: A worker directory for a block that has none, as confirmed by the human: the owner resolves it on its host, saves it and arms the fiber before launching. Blank counts as absent.

data.description: Base64 PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP bytes; at most eight images, 20 MB total.

images.description: Images attached to user_message; the owner stores them on its host and names their paths in the message.

example.user_message: Pick up from the plan in Status and run the tests.

200.description: A worker launched or took the message. session_uuid is the conversation id when the harness reports it at launch, else null.

400.description: fiber_id is missing, images are malformed or too large, or origin names no known host.

404.description: The owner has no fiber with that id (reason fiber_not_found).

409.description: A worker is already running (reason already_running, with its session, agent and timestamps), or an earlier launch attempt is unresolved (reason launch_reserved; retry with release_launch_reservation).

422.description: Nothing launched. reason is not_eligible (detail is homed_elsewhere, project_dir_missing, disabled, closed, no_shuttle_block or not_due_or_blocked), no_live_worker, arm_refused (needs names the field to supply), or a launch preflight's tag with message saying what to fix.

500.description: The launch failed; reason describes the error.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the owning host.

503.description: The terminal backend is not ready (reason backend_not_ready, waiting and retryable true), or boot is incomplete.

504.description: Poller did not answer; the launch may still occur. Inspect the fiber before retrying.

post.summary: Deliver text to a fiber’s worker.
post.description: Puts text in front of a constitution's worker on its owning host: a live worker is messaged, a dormant one resumes or launches with the text as its first message. The delivery field names which happened (message, input, resume, dispatch or context). delivered is true when the worker has the text, false when it did not get it, and null (with 202) when it was sent but arrival is unconfirmed; null is not a failure. Launch outcomes reuse the /dispatch envelope, so a launch refusal carries dispatched false and reason. context_only with message_id queues without launching (202). Error bodies vary: a validation refusal carries only error (and delivered false), a launch refusal the /dispatch fields, a forward failure reason and origin.

fiber_id.description: The constitution whose worker receives the text: its UID or namespace path. Named fiber_id as on /dispatch and /kill; /lifecycle calls it fiber.

text.description: The message; must contain non-whitespace text.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

from.description: Sender label shown to the worker, typically the sender's shuttle:// session address; blank or absent means "shuttle".

from_claim.description: Sender label, read only when from is "unverified".

context_only.description: Queues text in the fiber's context mailbox for its live or next worker instead of messaging or launching. Requires message_id; answers 202 with delivery context.

message_id.description: Idempotency key. Required with context_only, where the mailbox deduplicates by it; otherwise the receipt id when a live worker is messaged (absent generates one).

wake.description: With context_only: also starts a turn on a live worker (in a fresh session when that worker is at rest and costly to wake). Defaults to false, unlike /messages. Ignored without context_only.

unless_live.description: With context_only: when the fiber has a live worker, answers 409 with live true and queues nothing; otherwise the queued answer carries status queued_for_next_worker.

resume_mode.description: previous forces resuming the prior conversation (a live worker is still messaged); fresh starts a new conversation, stopping a live worker. Absent lets the owner message a live worker, or else resume or start fresh by its own rule.

message_after_launch.description: Sends text as a native message once the worker is up rather than in its launch prompt, launching first when none is live; waits up to 30 seconds for the worker's address.

live_input.description: Types text into the worker's terminal as the human's next turn instead of messaging it; with no live worker, resumes or starts one with the text.

reply_to.description: With context_only: the fiber the receiver should reply to.

notify_address.description: With context_only: the session address that receives the idle notice; defaults to from.

notify_when_idle.description: With context_only: subscribes notify_address (or from) to one notice when the receiving worker next goes idle or exits.

notify_wake.description: With context_only and notify_when_idle: the idle notice starts a turn for the subscriber.

thread_signal.description: With context_only: a thread lifecycle signal (uid, verb, stamp, owner) checked at delivery; Shuttle's own sub-thread reporting sets it.

retained_at.description: With context_only: the origin timestamp used to expire replayed thread context.

example.text: The review is in: tighten the error handling, then close.

200.description: The worker has the text: messaged (delivery message, with the receipt), typed in (input), or launched with it (resume or dispatch).

202.description: Queued in the context mailbox (delivery context), or sent with arrival unconfirmed (delivered null), including an owner that did not answer in time (reason forward_timeout).

400.description: fiber_id or text is missing or blank, context_only lacks message_id, or origin names no known host.

404.description: The owner has no such fiber, or (with context_only) no such constitution.

409.description: A live worker blocks unless_live (live true), the live worker has no addressable conversation yet or is no longer live, this daemon does not own the fiber, or a launch was refused as on /dispatch (already_running, launch_reserved).

422.description: The context mailbox write failed, or a launch was refused as on /dispatch (not_eligible, arm_refused, a preflight).

502.description: The worker rejected the message (receipt status rejected), the owner's answer was not JSON, or the request could not be forwarded (reason forward_failed).

503.description: The terminal backend is not ready, the local shuttle CLI could not run, or boot is incomplete.

504.description: The launch or message did not finish in time and may still happen; inspect the fiber before retrying.

post.summary: Send an idempotent message to an exact session.
post.description: Sends text to one exact session on any host. The address selects the host; there is no origin field. wake defaults to true. Reuse message_id with identical content to retry safely. HTTP 200 means the request was processed, not that it was accepted: read receipt.status (accepted, submitted, queued, context_added and subscribed mean taken; rejected means refused; unknown means the outcome could not be confirmed and the same request may be retried). Validation refusals return a plain Error; refusals from the receiving harness return a receipt with status rejected.

address.description: The receiving session, exactly as /peers lists it: shuttle://HOST/HARNESS/NATIVE_ID in canonical form. HOST routes the request; there is no origin field.

text.description: At most 65536 UTF-8 bytes, no NUL; nonempty unless notify_when_idle is true.

message_id.description: Idempotency key, nonempty, at most 256 bytes. Resending the same id with the same content returns the original receipt; with different content, 409.

from.description: Sender label, typically the sender's own shuttle:// address; one line, at most 1024 bytes, without [, ] or ;.

from_claim.description: Sender label, read only when from is "unverified".

reply_to.description: The fiber the receiver should reply to; at most 1024 bytes.

notify_address.description: Session address that receives the idle notice requested by notify_when_idle; defaults to from.

wake.description: true delivers the text as a task that starts a turn; false adds it as context without starting a turn.

context_if_busy.description: Requires wake=true. Lets a Claude session that is mid-turn take the text through its hook as context instead of a queued turn, and lets the daemon hold a message for an idle, costly-to-wake Claude session as context (receipt detail says so).

idle_only.description: Requires wake=true and a Claude or Codex session. Never steers an active turn: Claude queues the text for its next turn, and Codex refuses unless the session is idle.

notify_when_idle.description: Subscribes notify_address (or from, which must then be a session address other than the receiver) to one notice when the receiver next goes idle or exits. text may then be empty.

notify_wake.description: Requires notify_when_idle. The idle notice starts a turn for the subscriber.

example.text: Tests pass on main; ready for your review.

200.description: Processed; the receipt's status says whether the message was taken, rejected or unknown.

400.description: The request, address or host is invalid (Error), or the receiving side refused it (a receipt with status rejected).

409.description: message_id was already used with different content.

502.description: The owning host was unreachable or answered with a malformed receipt; the synthetic receipt has status unknown.

503.description: The local shuttle CLI could not run.

504.description: Local delivery timed out; the receipt has status unknown.

post.description: Runs one Shuttle lifecycle verb on the fiber's owning host. The fiber is named by fiber (not fiber_id as on /dispatch, /deliver and /kill), as a UID or exact namespace path. Each action reads only its own fields, listed on each property; a field another action uses is ignored. Required beyond fiber and action: repeat needs schedule and project_dir, set-model needs agent, set-outcome needs outcome, and role needs role unless clear is true. Success is 200 with the CLI's output as text/plain, not JSON. Errors mix media types: a local refusal or CLI failure is text/plain, an unknown origin is JSON Error, a missing fiber is JSON LifecycleMissing and a timed-out write is JSON LifecycleUncertain. When origin names another host, the owner's status and body are relayed as text/plain whatever their original type (a remote 404 arrives as text/plain carrying the LifecycleMissing JSON), except a retryable 503, which stays application/json.

fiber.description: The fiber to act on: its UID or exact namespace path (no leaf-name lookup). Note the name: /dispatch, /deliver and /kill call this field fiber_id.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

fiber_path.description: Exact namespace path of the fiber, consulted only when fiber is a UID, to pick the right document when several stores could hold it.

project_dir.description: Absolute worker directory on the owning host. Used by install, repeat, resume, reopen and set-agent; install requires it unless disabled is true, repeat requires it, and resume or reopen require it when the block has none.

model.description: Agent registry id to record on the new block. Used by install and repeat; absent uses the registry default.

agent.description: Agent registry id. Required by set-model; optional for set-agent, where absent or empty keeps the current base agent.

effort.description: Effort level for set-agent, a harness-native token such as low, medium or high; an empty string clears it, and absent keeps it.

schedule.description: Five-field cron expression. Required by repeat; optional for reshape to a standing kind.

tz.description: IANA time zone for schedule. Used by repeat (default UTC) and reshape (default the block's existing zone, else UTC).

until.description: For rest: what the rest lasts until, as a YYYY-MM-DD date, a fiber reference or free text; empty records neither. Must be a string when present.

review.description: For close: marks the close for the human's review, with the reason it is worth a look.

actor.description: For rest and close: the native session id the verb acts on behalf of; absent means no caller session.

role.description: For role: the office slug, or office/person, to set. Required by role unless clear is true.

new_name.description: For role: creates a missing role charter with this office name.

outcome.description: For set-outcome: the outcome text, written verbatim; may span lines. Required by set-outcome.

disabled.description: For install: installs as a draft (status open) that does not dispatch until resumed.

no_kill.description: For pause: stops future dispatch but leaves a live worker running.

tempered.description: For close: records the verdict, true for tempered (accepted) and false for discarded; absent closes into Awaiting review.

quiet.description: For close: delivers the outcome to the nearest orchestrator as context without waking it.

as_draft.description: For reopen: reopens to status open (a draft that does not dispatch) instead of active.

chrome.description: For set-agent: true enables the browser (chrome) axis, false clears it; absent keeps it. Claude harness only.

clear.description: For role and seat: true removes the role and seat (role) or only the seat (seat) instead of setting them.

action.description: The lifecycle verb. install and repeat add a shuttle block (oneshot or standing) to a fiber that has none; reshape changes an existing block's kind and schedule; pause stops dispatch and, unless no_kill, the live worker; rest parks the fiber in Resting and stops its worker; resume and reopen arm it again; close ends it, into review or with a verdict; set-model, set-agent and set-outcome edit one field; role and seat set its office; uninstall removes the block.

kind.description: For reshape: the target kind; absent or empty keeps the current kind.

200.description: The verb succeeded; the body is the shuttle CLI's output, which may be empty.

400.description: Unknown or missing action, a field the action requires is missing, kind or until is malformed (text/plain), or origin names no known host (JSON Error).

404.description: The owning host has no fiber with that identifier.

422.description: The shuttle CLI refused the verb; the text is "shuttle exited <status>: <message>".

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the owning host; the text is "forward to <host> failed: <reason>".

503.description: The write timed out (JSON LifecycleUncertain, retryable; check the fiber before retrying), the felt store registry is unavailable (text/plain), or boot is incomplete (JSON BootUnavailable).

post.summary: Stop a fiber’s worker without changing its lifecycle.
post.description: Hard-stops the owner’s live worker and tears down its runtime state, writing no verdict. Idempotent: a fiber with no tracked session returns killed=false with HTTP 200.

fiber_id.description: The constitution whose worker to stop: its UID or namespace path. /lifecycle calls this field fiber.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

200.description: killed is true with the stopped session, or false when no worker was tracked.

400.description: fiber_id is missing or not a string, or origin names no known host.

500.description: Stopping the worker failed; error says why.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the owning host.

503.description: Boot is incomplete or held; no action is attempted.

get.description: Reads the owner’s event projection newest-first; without session, repeated paths are deduplicated. With session, returns every send from that conversation; missing history is an empty files list.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: The fiber's UID. Sends match when the worker's terminal session name embeds this UID or the session ledger attributes the sending session to it.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: A native conversation id. When given, returns only that conversation's sends, keeping repeated sends of a path; it must be nonempty.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Send the ETag from a prior response. A match returns 304 with no body.

200.description: Up to 50 sends, newest first. Without session, each path appears once (its newest send). A fiber with no history has an empty files list.

400.description: uid is missing, session is empty, or origin names no known host.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the owning host.

503.description: Boot is incomplete or held; no action is attempted.

get.summary: Read artifact bytes from their host.
get.description: path must be absolute on the selected host, not relative to a fiber or confined to a felt store. Returns raw bytes with the file’s content type; conditional and byte-range requests are supported and forwarded to the owner.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute filename on the selected host.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Host id of the daemon that should answer; for a fiber or its files, its owner, as the composite row's origin carries it. Absent, empty, "local" or this daemon's own host id selects this daemon; any other value must name a remote this daemon knows (configured or discovered on the tailnet), and the request is forwarded there; an unknown name is refused with 400.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Send the ETag from a prior response. A match returns 304 with no body.

parameters.name: If-Modified-Since
parameters.description: Forwarded to the owner, but does not by itself produce 304; only If-None-Match decides unchanged content.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: A single range: bytes=start-end, bytes=start- (at most 4 MiB from start) or bytes=-suffix. Other forms are ignored and the whole file is returned.

parameters.name: If-Range
parameters.description: Use range only when the strong validator or date matches; weak tags cannot authorize it.

400.description: path is missing or not absolute, or origin names no known host.

404.description: File absent, unreadable or not regular.

416.description: Unsatisfiable byte range; empty body and Content-Range: bytes */size.

502.description: The request could not be forwarded to the owning host.

503.description: Boot is incomplete or held; no action is attempted.

ok.description: false on the endpoints whose refusals carry it (an unknown origin on /fleet); absent elsewhere.

retryable.description: true when the same request may be retried after a short wait.

ready.description: true once boot has finished and the daemon serves every route; false while booting or held. Readiness does not mean fresh launches are released from the boot quarantine.

kind.description: local for this daemon's own rows, remote for a peer's cached rows.

stale.description: true when the rows for this origin are not current: a remote that did not answer its last poll, or a local cache that has not finished a full poll. Stale rows are still served.

fiber_count.description: Number of rows this origin contributes.

last_polled_at.description: When a stale remote was last polled successfully; absent or null while fresh.

last_error.description: Why the last poll of a remote failed, or null.

cache.description: The owner's document-cache state (state is cold, partial or fresh), or null when unknown.

fiber.description: The fiber's frontmatter (and body when requested).

felt_store.description: The felt store holding the fiber, as a path on the owning host.

path.description: The fiber's Markdown file, absolute on the owning host.

dir.description: The fiber's directory, absolute on the owning host.

report_path.description: The fiber's companion report file (felt's report path), absolute on the owning host, when one exists.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that owns the fiber; pass it as origin on owner-routed requests.

orchestrator.description: UID of the nearest ancestor constitution that orchestrates this one, or null. Present on constitutions only.

column.description: The board column the owner computes for a constitution. Absent on fibers without a shuttle block.

turn.description: Whose move it is for a constitution: question, blocked and idle wait on the human; working and starting are the agent's; no-signal means a live worker reports nothing; none means no worker. Absent on fibers without a shuttle block.

runtime.description: The live worker's runtime state (session, phase, timestamps); present only while a worker is tracked.

pending_results.description: Number of results and messages waiting for this constitution's next worker: context its mailbox holds that no worker has taken, plus results addressed to it in the owner's outbox. Absent when zero.

dispatch_error.description: The last dispatch refusal or failure recorded for this constitution, when one is held.

origin.description: Host id of the daemon that owns the fiber; always present on composite rows.

PeerSession.description: Address and routing host are always present. Other fields depend on the owning daemon and harness; last_seen is epoch milliseconds.

polled.description: true once this daemon has polled the remote at least once.

stale.description: true when the remote has not answered its latest poll or has never been polled, so its cached state may be out of date.

terminal.description: Observed terminal holder; null when no holder has been remembered, including capture responses.

waiting.description: true when the terminal backend is still starting.

retryable.description: true when the same request may be retried after a short wait.

waiting.description: true when the terminal backend is still starting.

retryable.description: true when the same request may be retried after a short wait.

queued.description: Whether the text was queued in the context mailbox; false on every refusal.

live.description: true when the refusal is because the fiber has a live worker (context_only with unless_live).

killed.description: true when a live worker was stopped; false when none was tracked, which is not an error.

session.description: The stopped worker's terminal session name; present when killed is true.

SentFile.description: One file a worker sent to the human.

fullPath.description: Absolute path of the file on the owning host; read its bytes with /file.

timestamp.description: When it was sent, in epoch milliseconds; null when the event carried none.

sessionId.description: The native conversation id that sent it.
